An OpenTofu (Terraform) plan is about to be applied to an AWS account (one region). Running applications use these resources by name: they read and write objects, table items, queue messages, secrets and parameters, and invoke functions. Applying the plan carries out the resource changes below in dependency order. Replacing a resource destroys the old one and then creates the new one, unless the plan says the new one is created first (create_before_destroy). If a change fails, the apply stops there; the changes already made stay made.

Current state:
aws_s3_bucket.b: bucket vaws-s82-data; holds 20 objects; versioning never enabled; force_destroy = false in the state
aws_sqs_queue.q: queue vaws-s82-jobs; 30 messages waiting

Actions, in order:
1. Destroy aws_s3_bucket.b (it was removed from the configuration)
2. Destroy aws_sqs_queue.q (it was removed from the configuration)

How these resources behave: Destroying an aws_s3_bucket that still holds objects or object versions fails unless force_destroy is true in the current state; a force_destroy = true set in the same plan does not apply to that destroy. With force_destroy = true in the state, every object and every version is deleted first. Destroying an SQS queue deletes the messages waiting in it; a queue created by a replacement or under a new name starts empty.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
